revisions.title: Does the patient already have the cure?
revisions.body: Critias pins the charm to temperance and heaps superlatives on Charmides; Socrates adds the famous lineage. Asked point-blank whether he possesses sophrosyne, Charmides blushes and states his dilemma — denial insults his praisers, assent is self-praise — and Socrates converts the impasse into a joint inquiry.

revisions.title: A blush, a poet, and a borrowed answer
revisions.body: Charmides tries again — temperance as a sense of shame — then falls back on something he has heard: doing one's own things. Socrates insists the question is whether a saying is true, not who said it, and presses a literal reading under which a city would not be well-governed if each person made only his own things.
